description: When kids act out, parents might give negative attention, which can unintentionally strengthen those behaviors. Instead, kids thrive on positive feedback for good actions, guiding them toward better habits. By recognizing and praising good behavior, parents can nurture a constructive atmosphere. While withdrawing attention for minor missteps can work, it's crucial to stay responsive to genuine needs, striking a balance to improve interactions and foster growth.
title: Why kids repeat bad behavior for attention and what parents can do

description: Intelligence agencies are investigating pro-Khalistan groups recruiting within jails across north India. A recently detained operative disclosed connections to key figures while serving in Patiala jail. Agency investigations now focus on dead-drop recruitment methods and funding channels used by these groups. An SFJ-backed operatives was arrested after graffiti incidents linked to Khalistan activities. The arrested operative revealed a prior history of pro-Khalistan involvement and further recruitment efforts.
title: Khalistan groups turn to jail networks to recruit operatives across north India: Intel

description: ASML, Europe's biggest chip company, is currently selling no chipmaking machines in Europe, says executive Frank Heemskerk, blaming a lack of investment and zero new chip factories. CEO Christophe Fouquet and CFO Roger Dassen have also warned Brussels over AI regulation and tech sovereignty.
title: Europe's biggest chip company sells nothing at home, ASML exec says

description: Percival P. Baxter dedicated over thirty years of his life to creating Baxter State Park in Maine, now one of North America's largest state parks. His vision was to maintain the land's natural beauty, thwarting industrial encroachment and promoting sustainable forestry. Though he passed away in 1969, his legacy endures as the park continues to thrive, expanding through land trades and acquisitions to cover over 209,000 acres of pristine wilderness.
title: Ex-governor's 6,000-acre 1930 buy grew to 201,000-acre park gift by 1962
